lesson_title: Introduction to Halves Using Circular Cut-outs

studentJourney.title: Welcome to Halves
studentJourney.content: Look at the whole circle. In this lesson, you will split it into two equal parts.
studentJourney.owlText: Hi explorer! Today we are going to help Amina share a round chapati fairly. Ready?

mediaSpec.altText: Friendly owl mascot beside a whole circle, warm Kenyan classroom, clean modern childrens educational illustration, no text in image

studentJourney.studentText: Look at the whole circle. In this lesson, you will split it into two equal parts.

feedbackSpec.correct: Great! Let us explore halves together.

interactionSpec.prompt: Tap Start lesson when you are ready.

studentJourney.studentInstruction: Look at the whole circle. In this lesson, you will split it into two equal parts.

studentJourney.title: Your Challenge Today
studentJourney.content: Your challenge today is to learn what one half means and how to find it.
studentJourney.owlText: Here is your challenge! By the end, you will be able to show one half of a circle and explain what makes it a half.

items: Split it into two equal parts

studentJourney.studentText: Your challenge today is to learn what one half means and how to find it.

feedbackSpec.correct: Mission accepted! Let us begin.

studentJourney.title: Think First
studentJourney.content: Fair sharing means both people get the same amount.
studentJourney.owlText: Imagine you have one chapati and you want to share it fairly with one friend. Which picture shows fair sharing?

choices.label: Unequal pieces
choices.description: One big piece and one small piece

options: A
B
C
interaction.question: Which picture shows fair sharing?

studentJourney.studentText: Fair sharing means both people get the same amount.

feedbackSpec.correct: Yes! Fair sharing means both pieces are the same size.
feedbackSpec.incorrect: Try again. Look for the picture where both people get the same amount.

studentJourney.title: What Is One Half?
studentJourney.content: A whole is one complete object. When we divide one whole circle into two equal parts, each part is called one half. We write one half as 1/2.
studentJourney.owlText: A half means one out of two equal parts.

mediaSpec.suggestedVideoSearch: Grade 2 fractions halves equal parts circle

interaction.hint: A half needs two equal parts.
interaction.question: Show me.

studentJourney.studentText: A whole is one complete object. When we divide one whole circle into two equal parts, each part is called one half. We write one half as 1/2.

feedbackSpec.hint: A half needs two equal parts.
feedbackSpec.correct: Good. One half is one of two equal parts.
feedbackSpec.incorrect: Look again. The two parts must be equal.

studentJourney.studentInstruction: Tap Show me to see how a whole circle becomes one half.

studentJourney.title: Halves Around Us
studentJourney.content: You can see halves when one chapati is shared equally between two children. When the two pieces are the same size, each piece is one half.
studentJourney.owlText: We use halves when we share things fairly in real life.

mediaSpec.altText: A chapati cut into two equal pieces on a plate, warm Kenyan home context, clean childrens educational illustration, no text in image
mediaSpec.purpose: Connect halves to fair sharing in daily life.

interaction.hint: One half is one piece when the whole is divided into two equal pieces.
interaction.prompt: Tap one half of the chapati.
interaction.question: Tap one half of the chapati.

studentJourney.studentText: You can see halves when one chapati is shared equally between two children. When the two pieces are the same size, each piece is one half.

feedbackSpec.hint: One half is one piece when the whole is divided into two equal pieces.
feedbackSpec.correct: Yes. That is one of two equal pieces.
feedbackSpec.incorrect: Try again. Tap only one of the equal pieces.

interactionSpec.prompt: Tap one half of the chapati.

studentJourney.studentInstruction: Tap one half of the chapati.

studentJourney.title: Worked Example
studentJourney.content: Amina has one circular paper. She folds it into two equal parts. Then she shades one part. What fraction of the circle has Amina shaded?
studentJourney.owlText: Let me show you how it is done. Watch carefully.

steps.title: Amina starts with one whole circle
She folds it into two equal parts

interaction.hint: Watch how the circle changes from whole to two equal parts.
interaction.question: Next step.

studentJourney.studentText: Amina has one circular paper. She folds it into two equal parts. Then she shades one part.

feedbackSpec.hint: Watch how the circle changes from whole to two equal parts.
feedbackSpec.correct: Great. Amina shaded one half, or 1/2.

studentJourney.studentInstruction: Follow each step to see how Amina finds one half.

studentJourney.title: Your Turn
studentJourney.content: Practise showing one half of a circle.
studentJourney.owlText: Now it is your turn to practise finding halves.

interaction.hint: Look for two parts that are the same size.

studentJourney.studentText: Practise showing one half of a circle.

feedbackSpec.hint: Look for two parts that are the same size.
feedbackSpec.correct: Well done. You are showing one half correctly.
feedbackSpec.incorrect: Try again. Remember, halves must be two equal parts.

activities.prompt: Shade one half of the circle.
A circle is cut into one big part and one small part. Are they halves? Why?
activities.expectedIdea: No, because the two parts are not equal.

studentJourney.successCriteria: Practises shading, identifying, and explaining halves.

studentJourney.title: Think About It
studentJourney.content: Think about what makes two parts halves.
studentJourney.owlText: You have learned something important about fair parts.

feedbackSpec.correct: Good reflection. Halves must be two equal parts.

studentJourney.title: Lesson Complete
studentJourney.owlText: Great work! You can now show one half of a circle and explain that halves must be equal.
